title: Analytical Decision-Making Problems
tagline: Year 3 — Applying a set of rules to individual cases: eligibility checks, tiers, exceptions and missing data

introduction.overview: An analytical decision problem gives a set of rules (for admissions, loans, recruitment or scholarships) and a profile of a case, and asks what the decision should be. There is no hidden trick, only discipline: test the conditions in a fixed order, apply exceptions only when the rule says so, and notice when a needed fact is missing, because then the right answer is that the data is inadequate.
introduction.placementRelevance: Rule-based decision sets are popular in management and bank-recruitment tests, and they reward careful reading.
introduction.realWorldContext: Loan officers, HR screeners and admissions committees make decisions exactly this way.

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Both inclusive means the end values count. "At least 60" includes 60; "less than 3,00,000" excludes 3,00,000.

coreDefinitions: Knock-out condition: failing it means rejection regardless of the others.
Tier: a band of values that leads to different outcomes (for example credit score bands).
Exception: a clause that waives or changes a condition for a particular group.
Inclusive limit: the stated value qualifies. Exclusive limit: it does not.
Data inadequate: a missing fact could change the decision.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The rules are a flow chart in words. Walk each case through it, step by step, and stop at the first knock-out.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write each condition as a tick box. Test knock-outs first, then tier conditions. Before answering, ask whether any unstated fact could change a box.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Tiers
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Match the value to its band

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Exceptions
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Apply only to the named group

mainNarrative: A trust selects a student aged 18–25 with at least 60% in Class XII and family income below ₹3,00,000. A student aged 21 with 72% and income ₹1,80,000 meets all three and is selected. A student aged 24 with 65% and income ₹4,00,000 meets (i) and (ii) but has income in the ₹3,00,000–₹5,00,000 band, so goes on the waiting list.

Boundary values are the usual trap. "At least 60%" includes exactly 60%. "Less than ₹3,00,000" does not include ₹3,00,000, but "from ₹3,00,000 to ₹5,00,000 (both inclusive)" does. A student with exactly 60% and income ₹2,99,999 is selected.

An exception changes who must meet a condition. In the recruitment rules, a postgraduate need not meet the 55% marks condition, so a postgraduate with 48% can still be an Executive if the other conditions hold.
Tiers lead to different outcomes. With a credit score of 670, the loan is approved only with a guarantor; without one the application goes to the manager; at 640 it is rejected.
If a needed fact is missing, test whether it could change the result. A graduate whose marks are not given could be an Executive (with 70%) or be rejected (with 50%), so the data is inadequate.

deepDiveAspects.title: Order of checks
deepDiveAspects.content: Knock-outs first saves time and avoids contradictions.

deepDiveAspects.title: Over-reading
deepDiveAspects.content: Do not add a rule that is not stated, such as a preference for experience or a minimum for a field the rules do not mention.

solvedExamples.title: Boundary
solvedExamples.question: A scholarship needs at least 60% in Class XII, age 18 to 25, and family income below ₹3,00,000. A student aged 20 has exactly 60% and income ₹2,99,999. What is the decision?

solvedExamples.title: Exception
solvedExamples.question: Graduates need 55% marks but postgraduates need not. A postgraduate aged 32 with 48% marks and 2 years of experience applies for an Executive post (age limit 35, experience 2 years). What is the decision?

steps.title: Marks
steps.explanation: The marks condition does not apply to postgraduates.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The exception removes the marks barrier.

solvedExamples.title: Missing data
solvedExamples.question: A graduate aged 30 with 3 years of experience applies, but the marks are not stated. Graduates need 55%. What is the decision?

steps.title: If 60%
steps.explanation: The candidate qualifies as an Executive.

solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The missing fact changes the result.

traditionalVsShortcut.traditionalMethod: Read the rules once and decide.
traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Turn the rules into a checklist, test the knock-outs first, apply tiers and exceptions only where stated, and ask whether any missing fact could change the outcome.

commonMistakes.howToAvoid: Apply it only to the named group.
Check if the outcome would change.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options that contradict a knock-out failure.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Mark boundary words as you read.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Several cases share one rule set, so build the checklist once.

easy.question:
A trust awards scholarships under these rules.
(i) The student must be between 18 and 25 years of age (both inclusive).
(ii) The student must have passed Class XII with at least 60% marks.
(iii) The annual family income must be less than ₹3,00,000.
If all three conditions are satisfied, the student is selected. If conditions (i) and (ii) are satisfied but the annual family income is from ₹3,00,000 to ₹5,00,000 (both inclusive), the student is placed on the waiting list. In every other case the student is rejected.

Candidate: age 21 years; 72% in Class XII; annual family income ₹1,80,000.

What is the decision for this candidate?
easy.explanation: All three conditions are satisfied. Decision: Selected.

intermediate.question:
A company recruits executives under these rules.
(a) The candidate must be a graduate or a postgraduate. A graduate must have at least 55% marks; a postgraduate need not satisfy the marks condition.
(b) The age must not be more than 35 years.
(c) The candidate must have at least 2 years of work experience to be selected as an Executive. A candidate who satisfies (a) and (b) and has experience of at least 1 year but less than 2 years is selected as a Trainee.
In every other case the candidate is rejected.

Candidate: graduate; 62% marks; 3 years of experience; age 30 years.

What is the decision for this candidate?
intermediate.explanation: Qualification, age and experience of 2 years or more are satisfied. Decision: Select as Executive.

advanced.question:
A bank approves personal loans under these rules.
(1) The applicant must be an Indian citizen aged 21 to 60 years (both inclusive).
(2) The monthly income must be at least ₹30,000.
(3) The applicant must not have more than 2 existing loans.
(4) If (1), (2) and (3) are satisfied: a credit score of 700 or more means the loan is approved; a score from 650 to 699 means the loan is approved only if a guarantor is provided, otherwise the application is referred to the manager; a score below 650 means the application is rejected.
If any of (1), (2) or (3) is not satisfied, the application is rejected.

Candidate: an Indian citizen; age 35 years; monthly income ₹45,000; 1 existing loan; credit score 720; no guarantor is provided.

What is the decision for this candidate?
advanced.explanation: The credit score is 700 or more. Decision: Approve the loan.
